ADMINISTRATOR BYPASS GROUP
Users with this group have COMPLETE BYPASS of ALL warehouse restrictions: - Same permissions as before module installation - Record Rules do NOT apply - Python Constraints skip validation - Auto-assigned to base.group_system (administrators)
DO NOT manually assign to non-administrators. This would grant unrestricted warehouse access.

BASE RESTRICTION GROUP
Foundation for all warehouse restrictions: - Filters stock.picking.type by warehouse.user_ids - Filters stock.location by user.location_ids (blacklist) - Filters stock.warehouse by user_ids - Filters stock.picking by warehouse assignment
All restriction groups (Read Only, Send Only, etc.) inherit from this.
IMPORTANT: This group alone provides basic filtering. For advanced restrictions, use specialized groups that inherit from this.
ADMINISTRATOR BYPASS: - System admins (base.group_system) are EXCLUDED - NOT auto-assigned during installation (see hooks.py) - Record Rules only apply to users WITH this group

READ ONLY ACCESS
Inherits: Base
Permissions: - Can VIEW all assigned warehouses - Can VIEW inventory, pickings, quants in assigned warehouses - CANNOT create new pickings - CANNOT modify inventory operations - CANNOT create/edit/delete quants
Use Cases: - Auditors who need visibility but not modification rights - External consultants reviewing inventory - Reporting/analytics users - Quality control observers
Implementation: - Record Rules: read=True, write/create/unlink=False - Python Constraints: Skip (no modification allowed)

SEND ONLY ACCESS (Destination Only Restriction)
Inherits: Read Only → Base
Permissions: - All Read Only permissions + - Can CREATE pickings in assigned warehouses - Can SEND stock to ANY destination (no destination validation) - Can ONLY RECEIVE from assigned warehouses (source validation) - Can do INTERNAL moves within assigned warehouses
Restrictions: - CANNOT receive stock FROM non-assigned warehouses - CANNOT remove stock from non-assigned warehouses
Use Cases: - Regional distribution centers that send to retail locations - Central warehouses redistributing stock - Suppliers' internal logistics (send to customers)
Validation Logic (Python Constraint): ===================================== ONLY validate SOURCE warehouse: - WH1 → WH2: ✅ ALLOWED (can send anywhere) - WH2 → WH1: ❌ BLOCKED (cannot receive from WH2) - WH1 → WH1: ✅ ALLOWED (internal moves OK)
Example Scenario: ================ User assigned to WH_CENTRAL: - WH_CENTRAL → RETAIL_A: ✅ Send products (redistribution) - WH_CENTRAL → RETAIL_B: ✅ Send products (redistribution) - RETAIL_A → WH_CENTRAL: ❌ Cannot pull stock from retail - WH_CENTRAL → WH_CENTRAL: ✅ Internal moves

BIDIRECTIONAL ACCESS (Send + Receive)
Inherits: Send Only → Read Only → Base
Permissions: - All Send Only permissions + - Can SEND stock to ANY warehouse (no destination validation) - Can RECEIVE stock FROM any warehouse (no source validation) - Can do cross-warehouse operations as intermediary
Restrictions: - CANNOT create pickings in non-assigned warehouses - Source OR Destination must be assigned warehouse
Use Cases: - Hub/Transit warehouses that receive and redistribute - Cross-docking facilities - Central logistics coordinators - Inter-warehouse transfer managers
Validation Logic (Python Constraint): ===================================== Validate that operation involves assigned warehouse: - (Source IN assigned) OR (Dest IN assigned)
Examples: ======== User assigned to WH_HUB: - WH_HUB → RETAIL_A: ✅ Send (hub distribution) - RETAIL_B → WH_HUB: ✅ Receive (hub consolidation) - WH_HUB → WH_HUB: ✅ Internal moves - RETAIL_A → RETAIL_B: ❌ Neither is assigned warehouse
Difference from Send Only: ========================== - Send Only: Can send anywhere, CANNOT receive from non-assigned - Bidirectional: Can send anywhere, CAN receive from anywhere

FULL RESTRICTION (Source + Destination Locked)
Inherits: Bidirectional → Send Only → Read Only → Base
Permissions: - All Bidirectional permissions BUT: - BOTH source AND destination must be assigned warehouses - Most restrictive validation level
Restrictions: - CANNOT send to non-assigned warehouses - CANNOT receive from non-assigned warehouses - CANNOT do ANY operation outside assigned warehouses
Use Cases: - Standard warehouse operators - Location-specific staff - Users who should NEVER access other warehouses - DEFAULT for all new internal users (secure by default)
Validation Logic (Python Constraint): ===================================== Validate BOTH source AND destination: - (Source IN assigned) AND (Dest IN assigned)
Examples: ======== User assigned to WH1 only: - WH1 → WH1: ✅ Internal moves within assigned warehouse - WH1 → WH2: ❌ Destination not assigned - WH2 → WH1: ❌ Source not assigned - WH2 → WH3: ❌ Neither assigned
User assigned to WH1 + WH2: - WH1 → WH2: ✅ Both assigned - WH2 → WH1: ✅ Both assigned - WH1 → WH3: ❌ WH3 not assigned
Why DEFAULT: ============ - Least privilege principle - Prevents accidental cross-warehouse transfers - Administrators must explicitly grant broader access - Secure by default approach
To grant broader access: ======================== - Assign user to multiple warehouses: Full but multi-WH - Move to Bidirectional: Hub/transit operations - Move to Send Only: Distribution centers - Move to Read Only: Auditors
